svg.data-vd-steps: [[0, "How insulin works: a receptor with tyrosine kinase activity."], [1, "Insulin binds the outside of the receptor."], [3, "The inside parts phosphorylate tyrosines on the receptor itself..."], [5, "...and on other proteins, starting a sequence of reactions."], [7.5, "Vesicles carrying GLUT4 move to the membrane and fuse with it."], [11, "Glucose enters through GLUT4 by facilitated diffusion: blood glucose falls."]]
svg.title: Insulin receptor and GLUT4
svg.desc: Insulin binds the alpha subunits of the insulin receptor; the beta subunits phosphorylate tyrosine residues on themselves and other proteins, triggering a sequence of reactions that moves GLUT4 vesicles to fuse with the plasma membrane, so glucose enters the muscle or fat cell by facilitated diffusion.
svg.text: Insulin: tyrosine kinase receptor and GLUT4
A muscle or fat cell. Schematic.

g.data-info: A transmembrane receptor: two α subunits outside, two β subunits crossing the membrane. The inside parts have tyrosine kinase activity.
A protein hormone (two chains). It binds the outside part of the insulin receptor and stays outside the cell.
When insulin binds, the kinase parts add phosphate groups to tyrosine residues on the receptor itself and on other proteins.
The phosphorylated proteins start a chain of reactions inside the cell.
Vesicles carrying GLUT4 glucose transporters move to the plasma membrane and fuse with it.
More GLUT4 in the membrane → more glucose enters by facilitated diffusion into muscle and fat cells, lowering blood glucose.

g.text: more glucose enters muscle and fat cells (facilitated diffusion) → blood glucose falls
